cohort: The study included 270,329 singleton pregnancies with one prior cesarean birth (CB) and cephalic presentation undergoing a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) in the US national birth data.
finding: Interpregnancy interval < 18 months, induction of labor, and augmentation of labor were associated with increased uterine rupture rates, while maternal age < 25 years and gestational age at delivery 32-36 weeks were associated with reduced rates, and uterine rupture was linked to increased maternal and neonatal morbidities.
mod_finding: During a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC), an interpregnancy interval < 18 months, induction of labor, and augmentation of labor increased the risk of uterine rupture, whereas maternal age < 25 years and gestational age at delivery 32-36 weeks reduced the risk.
gest_age: Term and preterm singleton pregnancies, with gestational age at delivery 32-36 weeks and 37-41 weeks being specific factors analyzed.
